title: Staged shared-object prefetch and symbol quarantine for safer CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS upgrades
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Kernel compatibility regressions during CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA upgrades have resulted in intermittent inference failures in staging. Current startup probing pulls and links many .so artifacts at once which amplifies risk during phased upgrades. Goal: introduce a staged shared-object prefetch and symbol quarantine mechanism that reduces blast radius for mixed-kernel fleets and provides an automated rollback path when symbol conflicts or missing ABI compatibilities are detected. This reduces runtime flakiness during rolling upgrades and shortens incident MTTR.
technical_design: 1) Prefetch staging: implement a prefetcher that downloads candidate kernel bundles (.so) to a quarantine dir on the node and validates signatures and checksums before making them available to the loader. 2) Symbol quarantine: use dlmopen sandboxing to load new shared objects in an isolated namespace to detect missing global symbols or unexpected symbol re-exports without affecting the primary runtime namespace. 3) Health-shot validation: run a lightweight inference smoke test (short sequence length, small batch) against the isolated load to validate kernel entrypoints and math outputs within tolerance thresholds. 4) Promotion: on success, atomically symlink vetted .so into the active kernels path and update kernel manifest; on failure, discard and record diagnostics. 5) Telemetry: emit structured diagnostics (missing symbol names, unresolved relocations, checksum mismatch, smoke test diffs) to the console and runtime-telemetry pipeline. 6) Backoff/rollback: integrate with deployment controller to stop rollout on high failure rate and auto-rollback to previous kernel bundle.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary nodes): enable quarantine/prefetch on 3% of nodes in staging; monitor telemetry for 72h. Phase 2 (expanded canary): 25% nodes across two regions; run extended smoke tests and numeric-diff checks. Phase 3 (gradual): 100% rollout in staging, then apply to Dedicated test pool with reserved capacity, then to production with 1% increments and automatic stop on error threshold. Feature gate controlled via runtime-config flag 'kernel_prefetch_quarantine'.
testing_plan: Unit tests for prefetcher, signature validation, and quarantine lifecycle. Integration tests using a harness that injects malformed .so (missing symbol, bad checksum, mismatched C++ ABI) to ensure quarantine prevents promotion. End-to-end smoke tests with representative models (gpt-like and transformer-block-mems) and numeric-tolerance checks. Chaos test: simulate node restarts and concurrent promotions. Add CI job that exercises quarantine flow against a matrix of CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS versions used in our fleet.
acceptance_criteria: Prefetcher successfully stages bundles and rejects checksum-mismatched artifacts
Symbol quarantine detects unresolved symbols without affecting active processes
Smoke test numeric divergence within configured tolerance for vetted bundles
Telemetry surfaces clear diagnostic fields for failures (symbol names, binary metadata)
No production impact observed during staged rollout; rollback triggers on >2% canary failure rate

Implement dlmopen-based sandbox loader and symbol validation harness
Integrate smoke-test runner and numeric-diff comparator
Add manifests and atomic promotion path with symlink semantics
Hook telemetry and structured error events into Console and alerts

Run canary rollout in staging and collect metrics
